correctness.rationale: The n=4 proof was verified step by step with independent recomputation. Classification: brute-force enumeration of labeled graphs on 4 vertices confirms the 2-connected isomorphism types are exactly C4, diamond, K4. Groebner step: naive lex reduction of all 45 S-pairs per graph directly against the 10 nonzero 3-minors gives 0 failures and the lex leads match the reported squarefree monomials, so the minors are a lex Groebner basis and squarefree initial ideal implies radical. Irreducibility: X=U^T U surjects onto the sparse rank<=2 locus over any algebraically closed field of characteristic not 2; the constraint varieties (affine space; one quadric XY+ZW times affine space; product of two such quadrics in disjoint variables) are irreducible, the quadric by the singular-locus-is-origin argument, so V(I) is irreducible; radical plus irreducible variety gives prime over the closure, and contraction by faithful flatness gives primality over K. Target characteristic zero is included; general-n material is honestly labeled as evidence only.

originality.rationale: The EMERGENT_FINDING genuinely arose from target work (n=4 is the target's smallest nontrivial case, attacked with the target's Groebner-plus-parametrization methods), so there is no scope evasion; but full prior-art review defeats novelty. Deng-Kretschmer Proposition 15 proves in characteristic zero that for every n, I_3(X_G) is prime iff G is (n-2)-connected, which at n=4 is exactly the submitted primality claim, with the C4/diamond/K4 enumeration being elementary. The same paper's Question 16 poses the target question verbatim and records Macaulay2 verification affirmative for n<=6, so the n=4 fact was already recorded both as a proved theorem instance and computationally; Conca-Welker forest-primality plus transfer is the deeper prior implying it. The lane's delta (alternative self-contained proof, explicit S-pair certificate, incidental extension to characteristic not 2) is recomputation/certificate/parameter variation, which the STANDARD says cannot create originality; no literature search was performed in-lane.

value.rationale: Judged as mathematics in isolation, the headline is an exact, motivated local result of the kind the STANDARD's exact-invariant clause protects: the complete first nontrivial case of the admitted target and of published Question 16, with a uniform machine-checkable proof (certified squarefree degeneration plus rank-parametrization irreducibility) doubling as an explicit template for higher n, and honestly labeled general-n limitations. It is therefore independently worth retrieving in isolation; the fact that it was already proved is a priority defeat recorded under originality, not here.

checked_sources: Deng-Kretschmer, Ideals of submaximal minors of sparse symmetric matrices (JPAA 2024, arXiv:2211.07020): full text inspected, Theorem 1, Section 5.1 Proposition 15, Question 16 with Macaulay2 check for n<=6, references.
Conca-Welker, LSS ideals and coordinate sections of determinantal varieties (ANT 2019, arXiv:1801.07916): full text inspected, Theorems 1.1-1.5, Propositions 7.4-7.5, Theorem 7.8, Lemma 7.10.

Independent recomputation in this audit: naive lex reduction of all 45 S-pairs per graph against the 10 minors (0 failures), squarefree-lead confirmation matching reported leads, and brute-force enumeration of 2-connected labeled graphs on 4 vertices (types C4, diamond, K4).

broader_coverage.evidence: Deng Proposition 15: in characteristic zero with k=3, I_k(X_G) is prime iff G is (n-2)-connected for every n; at n=4 this is exactly 2-connected implies I_3 prime.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The headline's characteristic-zero content is a strict special case of a published broader theorem; the residual characteristic-not-2 extension runs the same argument with no new phenomenon, so broader coverage defeats originality.
broader_coverage.search: Stronger theorems on prime sparse symmetric determinantal ideals for all n with fixed minor size, including Deng Proposition 15 and Conca-Welker Theorem 7.8

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Headline: n=4 with every 3-vertex induced subgraph connected implies I_3(X_G) prime. Prior: arbitrary n with k=3 gives I_3 prime iff (n-2)-connected; for n=4 the hypotheses and conclusions coincide on characteristic zero.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior result substantively implies the submitted claim's substance in the target characteristic, so the submission is a corollary and repackaging of a known stronger fact with a new proof, and originality fails.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Literal comparison of headline hypotheses and conclusions against Deng Proposition 15 at n=4, k=3 and Conca-Welker Theorem 7.8(6)

equivalent_formulations.evidence: Deng Section 5.1 proves k=3 primality by noting the complement of an (n-2)-connected graph is a degree-at-most-1 forest and reformulating Conca-Welker forest primality; same objects under complement encoding.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The LSS and complement-graph formulations are not a different problem: the published reduction shows they substantively imply the submitted n=4 char-0 primality, so synonymous encoding does not escape coverage.
equivalent_formulations.search: LSS ideals, orthogonal representations, and complement-graph encoding of sparse symmetric minors with Conca-Welker transfer theorems
